clue.text: French fathers holding right to record company's first nights

indicators.note: the French fathers word clasps the next pieces, holding them inside itself

parts.note: peres is French for fathers
EMI is a well-known British record company

explanation.surface: Some French dads are clutching a contract for a record label's opening shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' places the right-plus-label pair just after the first letter of the French word. The possessive on 'company' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Premieres are the opening public performances of a show or film.

indicators.note: the answer is formed of letters within the phrase proper illumination, part of it

explanation.surface: A warning about the hazards of correct lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A peril is a serious risk or hazard.

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a claim is a miner's legal right to work a plot of ground

explanation.surface: A call to shout for the rights of a one-time miner.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, a synonym of shout.

clue.text: Where's the white van driver en route?

explanation.surface: A question about the whereabouts of a stereotypical van driver on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Transit is the classic British white van, so its driver is sitting inside one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a Ford Transit sits in that van; the idiom also means on the way, travelling between places.

clue.text: Slowing down has torn about everything, comes to nothing

indicators.note: the word for torn goes about, around, the word for everything

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, so torn
all means everything
comes to as in adds to, plus, giving and
O is the round figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone tears about, gets everything, and it all comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the torn word round everything to make RALLENT; 'has' is a link word. Rallentando is an Italian musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, rallentando is a direction to gradually reduce tempo.

explanation.surface: A pithy remark that an attempt fell short.
explanation.definitionFit: A coconut shy throw is an attempt or go; to be lacking something is to be shy of it.

clue.text: Start of sports transmission for child

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word sports is used here

parts.note: a prog is a programme, a broadcast transmission

explanation.surface: The opening of a sports broadcast aimed at children.
explanation.walkthrough: SPROG is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is informal British slang for a young child or baby.

explanation.surface: A cheeky, risque dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy Mexican sauce, so it is saucy in that sense, and also a lively Latin dance.

clue.text: Spain is sorry about some composer

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the run of letters is read backwards
only some of the letters of Spain is sorry are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: Spain feels sorry about a certain composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes INISSOR from inside 'Spain is sorry'; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian opera composer of The Barber of Seville.

parts.note: ginger is the colour of red hair
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A biscuit belonging to someone with red hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' splits into 'Red' and 'head'; the 's is a link. A ginger nut is a hard British ginger biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger nut is a crisp ginger-flavoured British biscuit.

indicators.note: about here signals the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a pianist's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a solo performance, typically by one musician such as a pianist.

indicators.note: performed suggests the letters are worked over, acted into another order

explanation.surface: A one-time leader carried things off with panache.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Yeltsin was the first President of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first President of the Russian Federation, a leader of the past.

clue.text: Pack animal left city with mother

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the city
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A beast of burden departed the city along with its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American camelid used to carry loads.

clue.text: Thirty minutes more play for the crowd-scene session

explanation.surface: A football match goes on for another half hour, like a long film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra time in a football match is two fifteen-minute halves. Extras are the background actors in a film's crowd scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Football's added period lasts half an hour; read as two words it is the period when film extras work.

clue.text: Such sweet delights relaxing in one?

definitions.text: Such sweet delights relaxing in one?

parts.words: Such sweet delights relaxing in one?
parts.note: the sweets are a jelly confection named after a country, and the steam room shares that national name

explanation.surface: A thought about confectionery taking it easy in a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turkish bath is a steam room for relaxing; Turkish delight is the sweet that shares its national tag.

clue.text: Young James is heard at the sports hall

indicators.note: is heard means the word is spoken and sounds like another

parts.note: Jim is the familiar short form of James

explanation.surface: A boy called James can be heard at the sports centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym, gymnasium, is a hall for exercise and sport.

explanation.surface: A haunted settlement that is completely deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooks are ghosts, so a spooks' town; a deserted settlement is one with no inhabitants left.

clue.text: Frank holds a performance of such ancient revels

indicators.note: holds means one word takes the others into its middle

parts.note: the Salian Franks were a Germanic tribe, so a Salian is a Frank
a turn is a performance, as in a music-hall act

explanation.surface: An honest person hosts a show of old festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' places the article and the act after the first letter of the tribal name. 'Frank' looks like an adjective meaning candid but names a member of a Germanic people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturnalia was the Roman December festival of revelry; the adjective describes that or any wild party.

indicators.note: about here means the letters are moved around into a new arrangement

parts.note: Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nation's fury concerning a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ANGER into ARGEN; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Eminent thought not in route (11)': OUT (not in) is plain, but 'thought' and 'route' give no STANDING and no anagram fits; likely OCR garble, no scan or search result gives the printed clue.

clue.text: Wrestling duo get a mat out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Wrestlers fetch a mat to perform on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag team is a pair of wrestlers who take turns in the ring.

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A man's wife is funny and attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit is clever humour in speech or writing.

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on groups of songbirds.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch is to keep guard over; a watch is the collective noun for a group of nightingales.

indicators.note: move tells us to shift the letters into another order

explanation.surface: An instruction to the cartoon dog Gromit to shift a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: Gromit is the dog in the Wallace and Gromit animations. The Tiger Moth is a 1930s British biplane.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Tiger Moth is a British biplane used for training pilots.

explanation.surface: The bread rolls belong to a car maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Rolls co-founded Rolls-Royce. Baps are soft British bread buns.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Rolls co-founded the luxury car maker; baps are soft bread buns, another word for buns.

clue.text: Memos showing the teachers' weekly is missing?

parts.note: no as in no paper, the publication being absent
the TES, Times Educational Supplement, is the British weekly paper for teachers

explanation.surface: Messages revealing the teachers' paper didn't arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British teachers' weekly; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are brief written messages, the same as memos.

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: loops are coils, turns of thread

explanation.surface: A reel winding up coils of thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a reel or bobbin for thread.

indicators.note: out of here signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A wading bird leaves its hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlap is to extend over and partly cover something.

indicators.note: returned signals the run of letters is read backwards
some indicates just a few letters lifted from inside golfer apparently

explanation.surface: A golfer seemingly gave back some of their score.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the standard score for a golf hole.

clue.text: Sneezing-and what is required, we told

indicators.note: we are told means the phrase is spoken and sounds like another

parts.note: a tissue is what a sneezer needs

explanation.surface: Someone sneezes and asks for what they need.
explanation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the British representation of the sound of a sneeze.

indicators.note: without means a letter is removed from the word
returned means the word for mariner is read backwards

parts.note: a seaman is a mariner

explanation.surface: A sailor came back without any active role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SEAMAN into NAMAES; 'without' drops an A.
explanation.definitionFit: Names and titles are both what something or someone is called.

clue.text: Tries to block genuine preparation for performance

indicators.note: to block means placed in the way, inside the word for genuine

parts.note: real means genuine
hears means tries, as a judge tries a court case

explanation.surface: A judge tries to block a genuine case of preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts but is the legal sense: a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run before the actual show.
